articleTitle: Basic features of MR clutches - resulting from different number of discs
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The main purpose of the paper is to determine basic features of MR clutches resulting from different number of discs N. At the beginning the authors considered the assumptions that must be fulfilled by the clutches (with different number of discs) which will be compared. Then 4 clutches (N=1, 2, 3 and 4) were designed with the use of computer program Agros2D. The 4 designed clutches having different number of discs were compared from viewpoint of the developed clutching torque T, the outer diameter, the external length, and ratio: clutching torque per total volume.

articleTitle: Impact of climatic conditions on PV panels operation in a photovoltaic power plant
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents an analysis of the impact of selected factors on operation of a solar farm located in Bialystok (northern east of Poland). The first part of the article discusses the climatic conditions specific to the area in question. The second part presents a set of results obtained in the solar farm. The farm is divided into two main sections: the first is optimally set on the tracker (a precise follow-up system) and the second is suspended on the facade of the building.

articleTitle: The influence of the damper cage on the waveforms and subtransient reactances calculated at a two-phase short circuit of a large hydrogenerator
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Influence of induced currents in conductive parts of the large hydrogenerator rotor on the waveforms occurring in the two-phase short circuit of the stator winding is investigated in the paper. The waveforms have been calculated using the finite element method with the use of a two-dimensional field-circuit hydrogenerator model. This model has been verified on the basis of the characteristics of idle run and three-phase short circuit calculated and measured in the power plant. Calculations of the waveforms at the two-phase short circuit have been carried out for various structural versions of the damper squirrel-cage, differing in the location of the eddy currents flow and the intensity of their interaction with the magnetic field. The calculated harmonic spectra of waveforms at two-phase short circuit have been used to calculate the subtransient reactances of the hydrogenerator. Comparisons and discussion of the achieved results are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of an auxiliary winding of a permanent magnet synchronous machine on the generation of shaft voltages
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents the concept of elimination of shaft voltages and shaft currents in permanent magnet synchronous machines. This method is based on the use of an additional winding to compensate for the time-varying circular magnetic flux present in the electromagnetic yoke. Based on laboratory measurements carried out on a prototype machine, the effect of an additional winding wound in the stator yoke on the values of shaft voltages and currents was examined.

articleTitle: Mathematical Study and Control of Diesel Rotary Uninterruptible Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The subject of the publication is recognition of the functions of the uninterruptible power supply system with a diesel engine called Diesel Rotary Uninterruptible Power Supply (DRUPS). The system features a diesel engine, a synchronous machine and an asynchronous machine as a kinetic energy storage and as well as two electromechanical exciters. In the paper a mathematical model of the DRUPS system was built and a typical work cycle simulated. Calculating the energy balance of the system resulted in the selection of its components at the design stage.

articleTitle: Natural Fault Tolerance of a Nine-Phase Induction Motor Drive Operating at Variable Frequency and Switched Supply Sequence
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents tests of fault tolerance of a regulated drive with a multi-phase squirrel-cage induction motor. The drive was controlled using variable frequency with switching the output voltage sequence of the inverter. The damages were mainly caused by break of one or several motor phase currents. The reason was bad inverter operation or phase connection interruption. Additionally, the effect of blocking a single transistor of the inverter half bridge was investigated. The faulty drive was to perform the same task of speed regulation as the healthy drive. The permissible extent of damage has been determined. The research was carried out in Simulink using the developed multi-harmonic model of a multi-phase induction motor.

articleTitle: Impact of climatic conditions and solar exposure on the aging of PV panels
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The article presents the analysis of the impact of location and climatic conditions on the operation and aging of PV panels on the basis of research conducted on the campus of the Bialystok University of Technology. The first part discusses the impact of location, arrangement and climate conditions on the operation of PV panels in the PV farm. The second part also discusses the impact of these factors on changing the efficiency of energy generation in the PV sections optimally set, in the sections mounted on the tracker (follow-up system) and in the sections suspended on the facade of the building.

articleTitle: Numerical Tests of Novel Finite Difference Operator for Solving 1D Boundary-Value Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The finite-difference method is an important approach for solving boundary-value problems of nonlinear ordinary and partial differential equations. In this approach, derivatives and partial derivatives are substituted by discrete finite-difference operators by considering the values at adjacent points, and finite-difference algebraic equations are developed. A large class of discrete operators exists and has been presented in many books on numerical methods. In the present study, an alternative approach to solving boundary-value problems is presented, which can be classified to a group of finite-difference methods.

articleTitle: 2D Discrete Differential Operators for Periodic Functions
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: This paper presents novel types of discrete differential operators for two-variable functions, periodic for each variable. They determine values of derivatives, both the first- as well the second, by the values of the function itself in a set of points uniformly distributed over the periods. Those operators relate the values of derivatives at each point to the values of the function in all selected points. Such operators allow creating easily finite difference equations for partial differential equations up to the second order, for solving boundary problems. They are addresses especially to nonlinear cases.

articleTitle: Limitations of control parameters of the three-phase voltage source inverter containing the soft switching system circuits with safe connections of capacitors and inductors
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Transistors of voltage source inverters are switched without losses when their currents or voltages are close to zero when the transistors are switched. This condition can be fulfilled by means of certain resonant processes, whose durations are comparable to the switching times of the inverter transistors. In order to minimize switching losses, the resonant processes cannot be interrupted before they are ended; otherwise such interruption may lead to a hard switching of these transistors. It causes some limitations of the inverter control parameters such as the amplitude modulation ratio and the switching frequency. Durations of the resonant processes are strictly related to values of inductances and capacitances of the applied soft switching system. The paper discusses influence of these values on the amplitude modulation ratio at the constant switching frequency; also limitation of the switching frequency for an assumed maximum value of the mentioned ratio is considered. Additionally, the inverter operation when the resonant processes have been interrupted due to a fault is discussed.

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation in granular metal-dielectric nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents the research of dielectric properties on alternating current of (FeCoZr)x(PZT)100-x metaldielectric nanocomposites. Tested samples with x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> = 51.7 at.% and x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 57.6 at.% have been prepared by using of ion beam sputtering technique using technological gases of argon and oxygen. After films manufacturing they were subdued to 15min isochronous annealing in temperature of Ta = 573 K. Alternating current (AC) electrical parameters of the nanocomposites: dissipation factor tgδ, capacity C, resistance R and phase shift angle φ have been measured for the temperature range 77 K - 373 K using frequencies of 50 Hz - 1 MHz. Based on the measurement results complex values of conductivity σ, dielectric permeability ε, electrical modulus M and their real and imaginary components have been calculated. Nonlinear dependence of conductivity σ vs. angular frequency have been observed for each samples. This indicates the hopping type of electrical conduction in the materials. Moreover, in both cases for angular frequencies ω <; 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> rad·s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> the ionic polarization takes place. This type of polarization is associated to the simultaneous movement of many atoms linked together by chemical bonds in the crystal lattice. On the other hand in case of frequencies ω ≥ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> rad·s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> the orientation (dipole) polarization is observed. In case of x1 sample one time τ dipole relaxation under Debye's conditions is registered. For the other sample x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, nonDebye relaxation can be observed. Values of the imaginary part of permittivity ε" increases when the real component ε' increases as well. In such a case, the dielectric response to the impact of external electric field E can be determined using the formalism of the electric modules M, which is a conventional method for analyzing of the dynamic aspects of charge transport in materials.

articleTitle: Concept of electromagnetic periodical duty pump with programmable liquid flow
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: In this article the trends in construction of electromagnetic driven low-power pumps and a literature review of several examples will be presented. The electromagnetic driven pumps will be divided according to their purpose and the type of used electromagnetic drive. The concept and spatial model of our linear electromagnetic low-power driven pump with programmable performance characteristics will be presented.

articleTitle: The protections of the 5 – node Medium Voltage power system in case of the symmetrical faults
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: In this paper the analysis of coordination between protection devices working in the 5 - node medium voltage power system consisted of 3 generators, sectioning π-type transmission line, and RL load in case of different fault location is presented. The measurements were taken in laboratory scale power system which can be used for future research of power system dynamic state.

articleTitle: Extended T(x) hysteresis model with magnetic anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper considers the possibility to extend a phenomenological hysteresis model to consider magnetic anisotropy of the material. The anisotropy effect is accounted by introducing modified values of some model parameters for different cutting angles.

articleTitle: Analysis of selected fault states of 12/8 switched reluctance motors
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Motors for critical drives require increased reliability. Switched reluctance motors are characterized by improved operational reliability. The tolerance effect, however, is partially dependent on the solution that is used. Designs with a minimum of four poles per phase are better suited for applications requiring increased reliability. This article analyzes selected fault states of a three-phase 12/8 switched reluctance motor. It is demonstrated that for the studied solution, damage to one pole winding allows the drivetrain to continue operating. The short circuit effect is manifested by a deterioration in the vibroacoustic characteristics of the motor (but at an acceptable level) and a decrease in the energy conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Field-circuit simulations of electrical asymmetry in double fed induction generator
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents the calculationresults of DFIGs in unbalanced steady-state conditions. The formulated 2D field-circuit model additionally takes into account a nonlinearity of magnetic core and a skewed rotor slots. Among others a short circuit in a part of stator phase winding was simulated and analysed. The spectra of symmetrical components of the currents show the frequency components characteristic for the introduced faults. In particular the current third harmonics resulting from magnetic core nonlinearity have been described.

articleTitle: Unified Power Quality Conditioner Controlled With the Use of Load Equivalent Conductance Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: In the paper a new method of controlling of operation of series-parallel active filters UPQC has been presented. The idea of load equivalent conductance according to S. Fryze is exploited in the paper. The presented method allows conventional compensation for nonactive component of load current and harmonics in source voltage together with improving the quality of the supply voltage, including sags and swells. In addition a case of pulse distortion arising in source voltage has been analyzed.

articleTitle: The Energy Conversion Efficiency in the Trolley Travelling Drive System in Tower Cranes
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper presents the experimental results concerning the determination of energy conversion for trolley travelling drive system applied in tower crane. The projected tower crane will be equipped in modern type permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). In the first stage of our research, the motor with the best functional parameters for cranes application from commercially produced permanent magnet synchronous motors was selected. The selection of the right PMSM was made on the basis of simulation calculations. Next, the test bench for determination of the functional parameters of trolley travelling drive system was built. The trolley travelling drive system consists of the PMSM, gear and power supply system. The special attention was paid on the energy conversion efficiency in proposed drive system. Selected results of experimental research for trolley travelling drive are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a smart lock system
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to present the design development process of an exemplary Smart Lock (SL) device. The scope of the presented study concerns modeling using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) software and laboratory tests as well as prototyping the control module (CM) module. Detecting the position of the actuating mechanism (plunger) was by monitoring the solenoid coil inductance. Therefore, coil inductance measurements were required with respect to the position of the plunger at various conditions of the AC component supply voltage. The energy saving and position monitoring functions were realized by using a micro controller with actuating elements. The proposed solution of the control module can be extended to other locking systems. It allows for the CM extension with new features and ensures connectivity with building automation systems.

articleTitle: PEF in food processing poles
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Pulsed electromagnetic field (PEF) is a relatively new, non-thermal food conservation method. It is uses the electric fields to eliminate pathogens and control food spoilage microorganisms. The chief benefit of this technology is the possibility of extending the shelf life of food products without using heat. Thanks to this, it is possible to preserve the right quality as well as nutritional and taste values. This paper is of revive nature. The article presents PEF technology and the possibilities of its application. The author works on the mathematical model of the product cell based on the long line model.

articleTitle: A Heating from a Standard Active Implantable Medical Device under MRI Exposure
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper, based on the technical specification ISO TS 10974, assesses the safety of Standard Active Implantable Medical Devices (S-AIMD) exposed to RF exposure of MRI devices at 64 MHz (1.5 T). A modelled implant has a form of a normalized wire lead that is typically used as a feeding electrode of cardiac pacemakers or deep brain stimulators. Such an elongated implant was placed in standarized tissue mim-icking liquid phantom. In the current investigation, the electro-thermal analyses of S-AIMD based on the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is presented and the temperature around the implant was estimated with the Fourier Law. In addition, the specific absorption rate (SAR) distribution on the axis of the wire-implant is evaluated and compared to the ISO standard. Importantly, the presented procedure may be helpful during the MRI exposure risk assessment for AIMD patients.

articleTitle: Methods of Preparing Soft and Hard Magnetic Elements by Additive Manufacturing — Review
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Applications of soft magnetic elements and permanent magnets increase due to broaden range of products with their usage. Nowadays magnetic elements are prepared mainly by casting, sintering or bonding technology. Presently research is focused on two ways: improvement of known magnetic materials and elaboration of new technology of fabrication magnetic elements. Development of new technologies enables obtaining magnetic elements with complicated geometry and can be made in a near net shape. These technologies that can be used are called additive manufacturing or 3D printing. 3D printing are divided in different methods. Article presents a review of different methods of 3D printing that are applied to manufacturing magnetic elements.

articleTitle: Influence of selected reduction methods on the cogging torque of multipolar machines with permanent magnets
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The paper discusses the problem of reducing cogging torque by combining different minimization methods. Cogging torque is the result of interaction between the magnetic field of permanent magnets on the rotor and the stator with variable magnetic conductivity depending on the angle of rotation. Cogging torque is of pulsating nature and occurs all the time when the machine is operating. It affects the work of the entire device cooperating with the machine causing vibrations, tensions and noise, breaking torque and thereby power losses leading to a faster wear of the machine's construction elements. High values of cogging torque cause problems with the regulation of rotational speed. Cogging torque impedes start-up of dynamos used in the wind power stations thereby making the activation of a power station possible only with high-speed winds. Due to these adverse phenomena the minimization of cogging torque in the machines with permanent magnets is a current issue and the most effective ways of dealing with the problem are highly desirable. Since the costs of prototype construction are very high cogging torque is minimized during the design process and by numerical methods. Computer simulations are used to determine the magnetic circuit with the lowest value of the cogging torque.

articleTitle: Estimation of Cumulative Action of Electric and Magnetic Fields near Electrical Objects
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: Electric and magnetic fields near electrical objects are very important environment factors which determinate possibilities of exploitation of areas near these objects. The complicated problem appears when the new object is planed in area with other electrical objects, because there are existing electric and magnetic fields and anticipated. In such the situation cumulative action occurs. The paper contains the problems with estimation of cumulative action of electric and magnetic fields near different electrical objects.

articleTitle: Reduction of Total Harmonic Distortion and Effective Source Current in Circuits with Nonsinusoidal Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: In linear resistor-inductor circuits, minimization of source rms current according to S. Fryze causes increase of total harmonic distortion (THD) and increase of source active powers resulting from higher harmonics of voltage and current. The authors of the present paper have proposed a method of the reduction of THD and rms value of the source current on the basis of the components of instantaneous power of the source. It has been demonstrated that the even component of that power secures a supply of the given active power from the source to the load. The odd component may be excluded from the instantaneous power of the source. Components of instantaneous power are the sums of the products of the even and odd components of source voltage and current. On the basis of these sums the voltage and current components have been determined, the compensation of which enables excluding the odd component of source instantaneous power, and in the same way- reduction of THD and rms value of the source current. The authors of the paper have presented the way of making use of the method in the situation when supply voltage is only odd or even function. It has been found out that it is possible to reduce THD of the source current several times in relation to THD of the source current while minimizing the source rms current according to Fryze, with negligible increase in the effective value of the source current in relation to the minimum value. Decrease of THD also causes significant decrease of active power of the source caused by higher harmonics of voltage and current.

Author Keywords: even and odd source power components

articleTitle: Control of prosumer energy sources in power grid feeded by three-phase distribution transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 15th Selected Issues of Electrical Engineering and Electronics (WZEE)
abstract: The co-operation of single-phase, prosumer power sources with three-phase grid powered by a distribution transformer Medium Voltage / Low Voltage (MV/LV), depends on the transformer windings arrangement and the control of the prosumers inverters. In the paper, the influence of the transformer windings arrangement on the flow of active power in a three-phase grid is discussed and the inverter control is shown, limiting the return of active power to the MV grid by the transformer. The control also reduces the power losses in the transformer and power losses in the MV grid. The transformer winding arrangement was chosen because of the possibility of transforming the energy from a single-phase prosumers source to the loads connected to the other phases of the transformer's LV side. Inverter control system was studied by simulation. Analysis and experiments are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed solution.
